issues.claim: The multilevel feedback queue was first developed by Fernando J. Corbató (1962).
issues.problem: Incorrect historical attribution – MLFQ was not first developed by Corbató in 1962; Corbató was awarded the Turing Award for the time‑sharing system, not for MLFQ.
issues.fix: Remove or correct the statement to reflect that MLFQ was introduced later in the 1970s by researchers such as C. A. R. Hoare and others, not by Corbató.

issues.claim: For this accomplishment, the Association for Computing Machinery awarded Corbató the Turing Award.
issues.problem: Misattribution – Corbató received the Turing Award in 1962 for the development of the time‑sharing system, not for MLFQ.
issues.fix: Clarify that Corbató received the Turing Award for time‑sharing, not for MLFQ, or remove the claim.

issues.claim: Give preference to processes with high I/O bursts. (I/O bound processes will sleep in the wait queue to give other processes CPU time.)
issues.problem: Contradicts standard MLFQ behavior – MLFQ prefers short CPU bursts and interactive (I/O‑bound) processes, but does not explicitly give preference to high I/O bursts; the wording is misleading.
issues.fix: Rephrase to state that MLFQ promotes I/O‑bound or interactive processes to higher queues, but does not prioritize based on the magnitude of I/O bursts.
